newsitem.title: SPAIN: Anti-NATO protest in Spain draws few.
newsitem.headline: Anti-NATO protest in Spain draws few.

text.p: About 1,000 Spanish communists and pacifists protested against NATO on Saturday in Madrid, three days before the alliance's historic expansion summit opens in the city.

The demonstrators denounced Spanish integration in NATO's military structure and shouted "Nato no, now more than ever". They invoked anti-U.S. rhetoric commonly heard in mass protests against NATO in the early 1980s.

"The United States, more than ever, is the policeman of the world and at most wants us to pay their fees," said Angeles Maestro, a deputy of the opposition United Left coalition. She questioned the need for NATO in the post Cold-War era.

Spain joined NATO in 1982 but stayed out of its military command structure due to strong popular opposition. But Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar received backing from parliament last November for full integration, a decision he will likely reaffirm at the July 8-9 summit.
Older communists mixed with youthful pacifists and groups supporting Iraq and Cuba at the protest march from Madrid's central bus station to the main square, Plaza Mayor.

At the same time, leaders of leftist and communist parties from Spain, Germany, France, Belgium, Portugal and England were meeting in Madrid to demand that Europe make creation of employment its top priority.
